description:
FOUND s438 (Opus 5) in the #473 cpan-t census population
(cpan-tests/modules/Text-CSV-2.04/t/01_is_pp.t lines 17 and 21, 2 drops).

REPRO:

  package C; sub new { bless {}, shift } sub module { "M" }
  package main;
  sub is { print "is(@_)\n" }
  my $csv = C->new;
  is $csv->module => 'M';        # perl: is(M M)
                                 # PCL:  statement dropped

The compiler's own message names the cause:

  PExpr: unhandled postfix '->' term ... term=PPI::Token::Operator "->"
         next=PPI::Token::Quote::Double "module"

`next` is a QUOTED STRING: the autoquote-before-fat-comma pass rewrote the
method NAME.  perl's rule is the opposite -- `=>` quotes a preceding BAREWORD,
and a word after `->` is not a bareword, it is a method name (the s407 review
fix already ruled that "a Word after -> is a METHOD NAME and ends a term" for
the term walker; this is the same fact, missing from the autoquote pass).

FIX SHAPE: the autoquote site must decline when the word's previous
significant token is `->` (grep for the sibling copy first -- memory says the
autoquote/callable classifier drifts into 2-3 copies, CLAUDE.md 11).

BAR: a Pl/t row for the method-name spelling plus the two it must NOT change
(`is FOO => 1` still autoquotes; `$h{-b}` untouched); census row for
01_is_pp.t leaves by EDIT.

DONE s456ag (Opus agent AG, round 13), TOGETHER WITH #482 -- and the task's own
guess ("grep for the sibling copy first") was right: they are ONE fact in two
passes, and both now ask ONE predicate, `Pl::PExpr::_word_is_method_name`
(an array + index; scans back over whitespace to the previous significant
token and asks `is_arrow_op`).

* #481: the fat-comma pass (`cleanup_for_parsing`, the `=>` -> `,` rewrite)
  quoted the Word to its left unconditionally, so `is $csv->module => 'M'`
  turned the METHOD NAME into a string and left the arrow with no word at all
  ("PExpr: unhandled postfix '->' term ... next=Quote::Double"), dropping the
  statement.  `=>` autoquotes a BAREWORD; a word after `->` is not one.
* #482: `extract_declarations` stripped `state`/`my`/`our`/`local` as a
  DECLARATOR, so `$one->state` reached the postfix-`->` handler with NOTHING
  after the arrow and the compiler died on `$nxt->content()` -- which is why
  the message named PPI's API instead of the construct.

The same fact already lived in the term walker (the s407 review fix); these two
rewrites read the word BEFORE anyone asks the walker, which is why the chain
`$o->thing` parsed and `$o->state` did not.

PROBES vs perl 5.40.3, 16 shapes, byte-identical output: `->module`, `->state`,
`->my`, `->local`, `->our`, `->print`, a keyword method name mid-chain
(`$csv->self->module`), the same six before a fat comma, and the negatives that
must NOT change -- `is FOO => 1`, `(-b => 2, key => 3)`, keyword-shaped
fat-comma KEYS (`module => 9, state => 10, my => 11`), `state $n = 0` in a sub
body, and plain `my`/`our`/`local` declarations.

MEASURED: corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111; emission A/B vs 83b335f over the cpan
+ perl-t + lib + board populations -- the movers are exactly
Test2/API/InterceptResult/Event.pm, t/Test2/modules/API/InterceptResult.t,
Text-CSV-2.04/t/01_is_pp.t and (on the board) Test2::Util::Grabber, RCDIFF 0.
Census rows for Event.pm (1) and 01_is_pp.t (2) left BY EDIT, and one of
InterceptResult.t's two.  Guard Pl/t/method-name-word-01.t (16 rows, 5 of them
negatives); on a base tree 18 of its rows fail.
subject: A fat comma after a METHOD CALL autoquotes the METHOD NAME: `is $csv->module => "M"` drops, because `module` is rewritten to a string and the `->` is left with no Word
